identity: A short Arabic children's-magazine comic strip (قصة مصورة). Line 1 is the series+episode banner (أبو الظرفاء / مطلوب شاهد = Abu al-Zurafa: Wanted, a Witness), line 2 is the credit block (سيناريو محمد قنديل، رسوم هانئ دراج), وفيما بعد at 134-135 is a caption box, and every other <NL> line is one speech or thought balloon. Plot: a father boasts he was first in everything at school, the son doubts him and advertises for a witness, the father's old friends (the judge, the shahbandar of the merchants, his friend Tufayl) turn up with the advert, and the father begs them not to tell the truth.
law: Balloon = utterance = sentence. Because each <NL> line is a single balloon or caption, the overwhelming majority of lines are exactly one sentence whose terminal ¶ is the forced pre-<NL> one, and nothing internal is marked. An internal boundary is admitted only where a single balloon demonstrably carries two or more complete speech acts: a standalone answer particle or exclamation followed by a fresh predication, a complete interrogative nominal sentence followed by a separate exclamatory list, or a formula repeated without any connective (أهلا X ... أهلا Y ... أهلا Z). Never split on coordination with و, on subordination (عندما, لأن, أن, ما), on a vocative tail (يا أبي, يا سيدي القاضي), or on a listing phrase (وفي الحساب وفي العلوم / في اللغة والحساب والعلوم). Header material is one unit per line: comic banners and credit blocks are separated typographically, by size, colour, column or dash, not by a sentence stop, so no boundary goes inside them. No <NL> token ever carries a boundary; every token immediately preceding an <NL>, and the final token, always does.
reasoning: I first fixed the genre, because it decides everything else. A banner line then a sceneario/رسوم credit line then a long run of very short lines, one caption box reading وفيما بعد, and a plot that only makes sense as panels, means this is a comic script with one balloon per line. That sets the default to one sentence per line and makes the real question narrow: which balloons hold more than one utterance. Then the contested sites. (a) i=1 الظرفاء: أبو الظرفاء is the series name and مطلوب شاهد the episode name, genuinely two title units, but a comic banner separates them by size and colour, not by a stop, and the corpus flattened no newline here, so the source really did have them on one line with no terminal punctuation. No boundary. (b) i=7 قنديل: the same argument for سيناريو محمد قنديل versus رسوم هانئ دراج, two credit items whose true separator is a dash, bullet or column, none of which restores as a sentence stop. No boundary. This is the site I am least confident about in the whole document; if this corpus does split credit items, this is the one I miss. (c) i=56 درجات: the one-sentence reading fails syntactically, because درجات نصف الدرجة is not an idiomatic noun phrase. The reading is the father exploding: أهذه درجات is a complete interrogative nominal sentence (are these grades), and نصف الدرجة في اللغة وفي الحساب وفي العلوم أيضا is a separate exclamatory list of the actual marks. Boundary at درجات, med. The list itself takes no internal boundary, since وفي ... وفي is one coordinated predicate. (d) i=88 طبعا: the son has just said مثلك as an incredulous one-word question, so طبعا is a direct answer and a complete speech act, with عندما كنت في سنك كنت الأول في كل شيء as a fresh assertion elaborating it. Against that, طبعا can be read as a sentence-initial adverb taken with a comma. I include the boundary but at lo only. My reason for including rather than dropping it is that an emphatic one-word answer in an Arabic comic normally carries its own exclamation mark or double-dot ellipsis, and both of those restore as boundaries, but the comma reading stays live. (e) i=140 القاضي and i=143 التجار: the strongest internal site here. أهلا يا سيدي القاضي, أهلا شهبندر التجار, أهلا صديقي طفيل is a complete vocative greeting formula repeated three times, and what joins them is repetition, not coordination, since there is no و anywhere in the line. Three greetings to three named arrivals are three exclamations. Both med, the only doubt being a transcriber who used commas. (f) i=170 عرضكم: أنا في عرضكم is the fixed plea idiom (I throw myself on your mercy), a complete nominal sentence, while لا داعي is an elliptical exclamation with its own illocutionary force. The decisive evidence is the next line, which is لا داعي standing alone as an entire balloon: this text treats لا داعي as a self-standing utterance, so it was one here too. Boundary, med. (g) Sites I considered and deliberately refused: ترى at 112 is a fronted wondering particle bound into the question هل يقول أبي الحقيقة أم لا, not a separate utterance; كل هذا لأنك لا تذاكر دروسك جيدا and عندما كنت في سنك كنت الأول في كل شيء are single complex sentences; يا أبي at 39-40 is a vocative tail on لا تقلق; في اللغة والحساب والعلوم is one list; ليس قبل أن أعرف نتيجة اختباراتك في المدرسة is one elliptical reply. Everything else in the document is a one-utterance balloon carried entirely by its forced pre-<NL> boundary.
